title: Dhamaal 4 Crosses ₹141 Crore, Becomes Ajay Devgn's 8th Biggest Hit
excerpt: The fourth instalment of Bollywood's beloved comedy franchise surpassed Singham Returns in under two weeks and is now inching toward the ₹150 crore club at the domestic box office.
body:
Key Takeaways
  • Dhamaal 4 has grossed ₹166.71 crore in India, nearing ₹150 crore club.
  • The film surpassed Singham Returns to become Ajay Devgn's 8th highest-grossing film.
  • With a budget of ₹150 crore, it has recovered 94% of production costs.
  • Worldwide gross is approximately ₹179 crore, with over ₹22 crore from overseas.
  • The film is on track to challenge Total Dhamaal's ₹154.30 crore for franchise lead.

Indra Kumar's Dhamaal 4 added ₹2.76 crore to its domestic haul on its 13th day of release, according to Koimoi, pushing the film's total India net collection to ₹141.28 crore. In doing so, the adventure comedy crossed the lifetime domestic total of Singham Returns (₹141 crore, released in 2014) to become Ajay Devgn's 8th highest-grossing film ever at the Indian box office.

https://youtube.com/watch?v=IG-eByZdz6Y

The film also edged past the lifetime collections of Dabangg (₹139 crore) and Gully Boy (₹139.38 crore), making it the 84th highest-grossing Hindi film of all time. India gross now stands at ₹166.71 crore, per box office trackers.

Second-Week Trajectory

After a strong opening week of ₹99.09 crore net, Dhamaal 4 maintained steady momentum through its second weekend, collecting ₹6.19 crore on Friday, ₹11.71 crore on Saturday, and ₹13.80 crore on Sunday. The weekday decline has been gradual: ₹3.31 crore on Monday, ₹4.42 crore on Tuesday, and ₹2.76 crore on Wednesday, representing a 16.6% drop from the second Monday figure.

TrackTollywood's granular data shows the film ran across 9,611 shows on Day 13 in 718 cities, recording an average occupancy of 8.4%. Mumbai remains the top-performing city with a cumulative gross of ₹14.86 crore, while Maharashtra leads among states at ₹35.57 crore gross.

Budget Recovery and the ₹150 Crore Target

Produced by T-Series Films, Panorama Studios, and Devgn Films on a reported budget of ₹150 crore, the film has recovered an estimated 94% of its production costs from domestic theatrical revenue alone. Bollywood Hungama projects the film's lifetime domestic net between ₹143 crore and ₹145 crore, though the current trajectory suggests it could push beyond that range with a decent third-weekend hold.

The next milestone on Ajay Devgn's all-time chart is Shaitaan at ₹151 crore, followed closely by Total Dhamaal — the franchise's third instalment — at ₹154.30 crore. Overtaking both would make Dhamaal 4 the highest-grossing entry in the Dhamaal franchise.

Where Dhamaal 4 Stands on Devgn's All-Time List

Ajay Devgn's box office record has been dominated by action dramas in recent years. His top three — Tanhaji: The Unsung Warrior (₹279.50 crore), Singham Again (₹270.60 crore), and Drishyam 2 (₹241 crore) — are all high-octane drama or thriller outings. Dhamaal 4's performance as a pure comedy, competing against those genre heavyweights, reaffirms the franchise's commercial pull among family audiences.

Worldwide Performance

Globally, the film has amassed approximately ₹179 crore in gross collections, with overseas markets contributing upward of ₹22 crore, according to BollywoodLife. Trade analysts expect the film to cross the ₹181 crore worldwide gross mark before its third weekend, which begins on July 25.

The comedy faces limited competition from other Bollywood releases in the coming days, though the arrival of major Hollywood titles in premium multiplex screens could eat into its urban share.

Franchise Legacy and Diaspora Appeal

The Dhamaal franchise, launched in 2007, has been a reliable comedy brand across the Indian diaspora, with its physical humour and ensemble energy translating well beyond Hindi-belt audiences. The fourth instalment brings back the core trio of Ajay Devgn, Arshad Warsi, and Riteish Deshmukh alongside Jaaved Jaaferi, Sanjay Mishra, and Ravi Kishan, with Esha Gupta and Sanjeeda Shaikh joining the cast.

With no major Bollywood competitor on the horizon, Dhamaal 4 is expected to hold screens through the coming weekend. Whether it can challenge Total Dhamaal's ₹154.30 crore to claim the franchise crown will depend on its third-weekend hold and how long multiplexes keep it in prime slots.
